chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Nu'aym al-Azdi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about four witnesses who testified against a man for adultery. So when he was killed, one of them retracted from his testimony.
He said: So he (the Imam) said: The fourth shall be killed, and the three shall pay to his family three-quarters of the blood money (diya).

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Diya — blood money or wergild, the financial compensation paid to the family of a wrongfully killed person
key_terms.الزِّنَى: Adultery/zina — one of the grave sins (kaba'ir) requiring four witnesses for conviction under hadd punishment
key_terms.رَجَعَ عَنْ شَهَادَتِهِ: Retraction of testimony — nullifying previously given testimony, which in this case makes the witness liable as a false accuser
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Testimony/witness — in Islamic law, false testimony in a capital case carries severe consequences

ai.seo_question: What happens according to Imam al-Sadiq when a witness retracts their adultery testimony after the accused is executed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a specific legal scenario in Islamic criminal law (hudud): when four witnesses testify to adultery and the convicted man is executed, but one witness later retracts. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the retracting witness bears full criminal liability (to be killed as a false accuser who caused an unjust death), while the other three, whose partial false testimony contributed to the execution, must pay three-quarters of the diya (blood money) to the victim's family. This ruling reflects the strict accountability attached to testimony in capital cases.
